$comment: Street-name normalisation rules — SPEC.md §4.3.
This file is the SINGLE SOURCE of those rules. It is read by the index
generation script (tools/build_address_index.py) AND embedded in the APK,
where the search engine reads it again. A divergence between the two would
make streets unfindable: "boulevard" indexed on one side, "bd" searched
on the other, and no result. Hence the shared file rather than two copied
lists.
Normalisation is applied identically to the index and to what is typed:
lower case, accents and punctuation removed, abbreviations expanded.
tools/build_address_index.py also produces a set of reference cases that
the Kotlin test replays, to prove that the two implementations give the
same result.
Expanded during normalisation, on whole words only.
A single-letter abbreviation is expanded only at the head of a name,
otherwise "r" would turn "Jean R Dupont" into "Jean rue Dupont".
The street type is stored in a field SEPARATE from the proper name
(§4.3): "gambetta" must find "rue Gambetta", and "rue de la gare" must
not be penalised by word order.
Recognised only at the head of a name, and by longest match: "rond
point" before "rond". "drève" and "courée" belong to the North of
France and are absent from generic lists.
Written in their already normalised form (no accent, lower case).
Stop words ignored when RANKING — never when indexing, otherwise
"rue de la gare" would lose half its content. They serve not to reward
a match that only bears on "de" or "la".
